events.title: Octavian defeats Antony and Cleopatra at Actium
events.description: Octavian's fleet under Agrippa defeated Mark Antony and Cleopatra off Actium in western Greece. Their flight to Egypt left Octavian, soon to be Augustus, master of the Roman world.
events.html: Octavian's fleet under Agrippa defeated Mark Antony and Cleopatra off Actium in western Greece. Their flight to Egypt left Octavian, soon to be Augustus, master of the Roman world.

events.title: The Great Fire of London breaks out in Pudding Lane
events.description: Fire broke out in Thomas Farriner's bakery and raged for four days, destroying some 13,200 houses, 87 churches and old St Paul's Cathedral. Wren's rebuilding transformed the City.
events.html: Fire broke out in Thomas Farriner's bakery and raged for four days, destroying some 13,200 houses, 87 churches and old St Paul's Cathedral. Wren's rebuilding transformed the City.

events.title: The September Massacres begin in Paris
events.description: Fearing a Prussian advance and a plot among prisoners, crowds broke into Paris prisons and killed some 1,100 to 1,400 inmates over five days. The massacres foreshadowed the Terror.
events.html: Fearing a Prussian advance and a plot among prisoners, crowds broke into Paris prisons and killed some 1,100 to 1,400 inmates over five days. The massacres foreshadowed the Terror.

events.title: Japan signs the instrument of surrender aboard USS Missouri
events.description: Japanese envoys signed the formal surrender in Tokyo Bay before General MacArthur and Allied representatives. The ceremony officially ended the Second World War.
events.html: Japanese envoys signed the formal surrender in Tokyo Bay before General MacArthur and Allied representatives. The ceremony officially ended the Second World War.

events.title: CBS Evening News becomes America's first half-hour network newscast
events.description: Walter Cronkite's evening news on CBS expanded from 15 to 30 minutes, opening with an interview with President Kennedy. NBC followed within a week, setting the format of US network news.
events.html: Walter Cronkite's evening news on CBS expanded from 15 to 30 minutes, opening with an interview with President Kennedy. NBC followed within a week, setting the format of US network news.
